title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: Atomically precise polynuclear metal clusters are useful model catalysts for water splitting and CO2 conversion because their defined structures allow structure–property analysis and because multiple metal centers can act cooperatively in multielectron reactions.
explanation: The introduction contrasts clusters with aggregated nanoparticles and mononuclear complexes, and notes that enzymatic {NiFe} hydrogenase and {CaMn4O5} water-oxidation sites motivate artificial lanthanide-containing clusters (LnCCs), including 3d–4f clusters, cluster-based MOFs, and composites.
scope: Polynuclear metal clusters, especially lanthanide-only and lanthanide–transition-metal clusters used for HER, OER, and CO2 conversion.
caveats: This is a framing argument; the review does not claim every polynuclear cluster is more active than the corresponding mononuclear complex.
